title: Convert the PRD to a spec

levels.label: Nudge
levels.text: Decide the shape of one requirement before you ask for eight: an ID, a one-line statement, then at least one Given / When / Then. Then the parts around them that a spec needs: what is out of scope, what you could not test, who owns it, and a changelog.

levels.label: Approach
levels.text:
Ask Claude to convert the PRD section by section, and to FLAG any sentence it cannot test instead of guessing what it means. Section 9 of the PRD has four such sentences.

A spec records what is WANTED, so it includes the requirements the code does not meet yet. Commit the first draft as it is, before you improve it: the next milestone needs the history.

levels.label: Near-solution
levels.text:
Eight requirements, one for each of sections 1 to 8, in the PRD's order (REQ-001 to REQ-008). A criterion with a number in it ("a store with 3 units and a customer who wants 1") can be turned into a test. One without ("enough stock") can only be argued about.

The parts around them are headings: Non-goals (the PRD lists what is out of scope), Flagged: too vague to test (the four sentences, each with the question you would ask), and Changelog. Put "Owner: <a name>" near the top.

reveal.referenceBrief:
CONTEXT: docs/prd.md is the product requirements for BOPIS eligibility (sections 1 to 8 are rules, section 9 is general remarks, section 10 is out of scope). My drift report is in docs/drift-report.md.

TASK: Convert the PRD into spec/bopis-eligibility.md.

CONSTRAINTS: One "## REQ-00N: title" heading for each rule in sections 1 to 8, numbered in the PRD's order. Under each heading: a one-line statement, then Given / When / Then acceptance criteria, each precise enough to write a test from (use numbers). Include the requirements the code does not meet yet. Do not guess what a vague sentence means: put it under "Flagged: too vague to test" with the question it raises, and do not make it a requirement. Do not invent requirements the PRD does not have.

ACCEPTANCE: Non-goals from section 10; an "Owner:" line; a Changelog with the first entry; the four vague sentences of section 9 flagged.

VERIFY: Read each requirement against the PRD. Then npm run step -- 2, and commit the draft before you change it.
reveal.approach:
The structured spec is the intermediate step the deck insists on: generating code straight from PRD prose gives vague code faster. The three habits of this milestone are IDs that never change, criteria you could write a test from, and flagged questions instead of confident guesses.

The first draft will contain a guess. Do not fix it yet: commit it, so that the history shows what the AI wrote and what a person changed.
commonMistakes: Turning "eligibility checks should be fast" into a requirement. It cannot be tested as written.
Leaving out the requirements the code does not meet (a spec that only describes the code is documentation, not a spec).
Criteria without numbers ("enough stock", "heavy"), which cannot become a test.
No Non-goals, so the AI is free to build substitutions and delivery.
Fixing the draft before the first commit, so the history never shows the AI's version.
Renumbering the requirements later: an ID is stable, it names one requirement forever.
